correctness.rationale: For each d>=3 with q_i>=2 and max q_i>=3, the forbidden-triple definition forces any dual face with a nonadjacent pair into its unique axis-parallel square, while clique faces lie in coordinate lines. The dual comprises these line simplices, Q rectangle tetrahedra and exactly a isolated long-distance edges. Each tetrahedron collapses relative to its four-edge perimeter to a square disk. The line union B has H1 free of rank L-N+1. The product-of-simplices two-skeleton proves simply connectivity after all Q squares; the integral pair exact sequence forces H2 free of rank Q-(L-N+1)=b. Whitehead yields a wedge of b 2-spheres; the a additional edges supply a circles. Integral Alexander duality gives precisely H_(N-5)=Z^b and H_(N-4)=Z^a. Seven independent finite face enumerations and complete modular boundary computations passed; finite checks are explicitly not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic searches of published mathematical records, accessible prior claims and source full texts reveal two-factor rook, all-binary hypercube, and one ternary three-cube results, but not the unified arbitrary heterogeneous factor theorem. The theorem makes genuinely new predictions in the disjoint mixed domain d>=3 with max(q_i)>=3. Foundational papers cover graph joins/clique prisms/path grids; another recent paper treats total two-cut rather than ordinary three-cut. Full-text and source-scope comparisons below distinguish implication, not only terminology. Residual risk from unindexed material is recorded.

value.rationale: The arbitrary mixed-alphabet Cartesian-clique products are natural Hamming graphs and form an infinite, genuinely multi-parameter class. The theorem determines all reduced integral homology and a dual homotopy type; the two ranks encode different geometric mechanisms (rectangle two-cycles and Hamming distance>=3 edges). It proves nonshellability uniformly and recovers different previously isolated boundary phenomena without merely recomputing an existing table. The previously uncovered 12-vertex K2 square K2 square K3 instance has two nonzero ranks 6 and 12, and the structural proof covers every larger mixed tuple.
